title: Exclusive | Quantum Startup Oratomic Now Worth $5.4 Billion After Series-B Funding
source_used: SiliconANGLE (relaying the Wall Street Journal exclusive; WSJ page returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: Oratomic, a California quantum computing company founded in 2025, raised $475 million in a Series B round.
ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions co-led the round.
The round came three months after a $300 million Series A and brings total funding to $775 million.
SiliconANGLE puts the valuation at $5.5 billion, up from $1.5 billion; the WSJ headline says $5.4 billion.
Oratomic uses reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays and aims to do error correction with about 10,000 qubits, against roughly 1 million that industry standards often assume.
CEO Dolev Bluvstein told the WSJ the business models and applications are not yet known; the need is a cheap, manufacturable working computer.
quote_evidence: California-based Oratomic, which uses reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays, raised $475 million, while United Kingdom-based Universal Quantum Ltd., which develops modular trapped-ion systems, raised more than $100 million in Series A funding.
The investment brings the company's total funding to date to $775 million and raised its valuation to $5.5 billion from $1.5 billion.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors more than tripled the startup's valuation in three months on a bet about low-qubit error correction.
notes: WSJ original blocked (HTTP 401, paywall). Read SiliconANGLE, which cites the WSJ interview. Valuation differs slightly: $5.4 billion in the WSJ headline, $5.5 billion in SiliconANGLE. Wilson Sonsini (law firm) also announced advising on a $475 million Series B (headline only).
